items.title: Sessions and memory (State and context management) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 05
items.summary: This Level 300 deck shows how to give a Strands Agents agent memory: the conversation history and agent.state, snapshots, a SnapshotSessionManager with a Storage that continues after a restart, a MemoryManager that carries knowledge across sessions, and context_manager and conversation managers that keep the conversation inside the context window. It uses the official docs, architecture diagrams, and real output of a help-desk agent run on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region, as deck 05 (Go deeper) of the series Learn Strands Agents with Kiro.

items.title: Multi-agent (Agents as tools, Swarm, Graph, and A2A) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 07
items.summary: This Level 300 deck shows five ways to combine agents in Strands Agents (1.64), following the chapters of the official docs, with the code of a help desk agent and real output from Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region. It covers passing an agent as a tool (as_tool, delegate), Swarm and Graph (handoffs, conditional edges, the OR default, loop limits), Workflow, A2AAgent and A2AServer, and human approval with an interrupt in BeforeNodeCallEvent, as deck 07 (Go deeper) of the series Learn Strands Agents with Kiro.

items.title: Let it compute and browse (Code Interpreter and Browser) | Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro 05
items.summary: This Level 300 deck shows how to give an agent two built-in tools of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Code Interpreter, which runs Python in a sandbox environment so that sums are exact instead of guessed by the model, and Browser, which opens a web page that has no API in an isolated browser driven with Playwright through the Automation endpoint, while a person can watch and take over through the Live View endpoint. On the help desk agent of a made-up online electronics shop, deployed to the Tokyo Region, it totals the refunds of 12 returns, reads a delivery date from a carrier tracking page, compares Gateway, Code Interpreter and Browser, covers the cautions for outside pages, generated code and irreversible actions, and stops the sessions afterward, shown with figures of what happened and real terminal output, as deck 05 (Build it out) of the series Learn Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Kiro.

items.title: Keep improving the harness (So the same miss doesn't happen twice) | Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro 08
items.summary: A Level 200 deck on keeping a harness improving with Kiro: log each miss in one line, turn a repeated or costly miss into steering, a hook, or a skill, check whether it worked, watch for slow drift on a schedule, and take away mechanisms that stop helping, based on public articles from OpenAI, Anthropic, martinfowler.com, Mitchell Hashimoto, and the kiro.dev blog. On a small meeting-room booking app made for this series, real Kiro CLI 3.1 screens show Kiro proposing mechanisms from the miss log, asking before it writes a file, keeping a property-based test's counterexample as a regular test, writing a skill's common mistakes, and saving a memory you can open and read. This is deck 08 (Run the loop pillar) of the "Learn Harness Engineering with Kiro" series.
